content.text: The infrastructure problem is not just about [[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/how-accepting-bitcoin-ebook-sales-works-how-deploy-3|accepting]] payments; it's about being able to reach your global audience. As a Venezuelan creator, you face unique challenges in accepting payments for [[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/digital-product-payment-solutions-west-africa-minimum-viable-2|Digital Product]] products due to stringent international sanctions and traditional payment gatekeepers like Stripe that refuse service. This leaves many digital product sellers, including authors, course creators, and software developers, unable to reach their global audience. Coremerch provides an infrastructure solution to bypass these restrictions, enabling creators to accept crypto payments from international buyers.

This post is part of the COREMERCH infrastructure series. For the complete foundation — every component, every configuration step, and the full deployment sequence — read the pillar guide: Selling Digital Products from Africa: The Complete Infrastructure Guide at https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/selling-digital-products-africa-step-step-deployment-guide. That guide covers the complete architecture that this post builds on.

content.text: What You Can Actually Get Done Today

With the right infrastructure, you can set up a secure and reliable payment system for your digital products in under an hour. By leveraging NOWPayments and [[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/cloudflare-r2-digital-product-storage-delivery-what-actually-6|COREMERCH guide to cloudflare]] infrastructure, you can accept a wide range of cryptocurrencies, including USDT on Tron, which settles in under 60 seconds for a fee under $0.10. This means you can focus on creating and marketing your digital products without worrying about payment processing issues.
The Minimum Viable Stack That Works

The Edge Commerce Stack is the minimum viable stack that works for most creators. This stack includes GitHub Pages or Cloudflare Pages for hosting, Cloudflare Workers or Google Apps Script for backend logic, Supabase or Google Sheets for order storage, Google Drive or Cloudflare R2 for file delivery, and NOWPayments for automatic on-chain crypto payment verification. This stack can be deployed in under 48 hours and comes with 30-day support.
Skipping the Steps That Do Not Matter Yet

Cloudflare Pages and GitHub Pages both provide free static site hosting that works identically regardless of where the store operator is located. A store deployed on Cloudflare Pages by a creator in Harare is served from Cloudflare's global edge network — the same infrastructure that serves enterprises in New York. Neither platform imposes geographic restrictions on who can deploy a store or who can access it. Combined with NOWPayments for payment processing and Cloudflare Workers or Google Apps Script for backend logic, this creates a complete commerce infrastructure with zero hosting costs and no geographic restrictions at any layer of the stack.
The Edge Commerce Stack is the minimum viable stack that works for most creators.
Getting Your First Transaction Live

Creators in Ethiopia, Cameroon, Tanzania, Venezuela, Zimbabwe, and the Philippines face a compounded challenge: not only are conventional payment platforms unavailable, but local banking infrastructure may add additional friction to receiving international transfers through alternative channels. Crypto payments remove this layer entirely. A seller in Addis Ababa and a seller in Amsterdam receive USDT transactions through the same NOWPayments infrastructure, at the same speed, with the same 0.5% fee. The blockchain has no knowledge of which country a wallet is located in. The webhook fires to both backends identically. Geographic neutrality is not a feature — it is the fundamental property of how blockchains work.
What to Do in the Next 24 Hours

In the next 24 hours, focus on deploying the Edge Commerce Stack and setting up payment processing. This includes hosting your digital products on GitHub Pages or Cloudflare Pages, setting up backend logic with Cloudflare Workers or Google Apps Script, and configuring order storage with Supabase or Google Sheets. By the end of the day, you should have a working payment system and be ready to start accepting transactions.
How can creators in Africa sell digital products to international buyers?

The most practical path for creators in restricted countries starts with NOWPayments configured to receive USDT on Tron as the primary payment coin. USDT is a stable coin pegged to the US dollar — your revenue does not fluctuate with crypto market movements. Tron network fees are under $0.10, and settlement takes under 60 seconds. Once USDT arrives in your wallet, you convert to local currency through P2P exchanges — Binance P2P is available in most countries and supports naira, cedis, Kenyan shillings, and Pakistani rupees. The conversion takes 20 to 30 minutes on average and costs 2 to 5 percent.
NOWPayments supports a wide range of cryptocurrencies, including USDT on Tron.

This kit includes all 6 blueprints and 7 templates and can be downloaded instantly. Your Deployment Checklist

Confirm which cryptocurrencies have the best P2P conversion options in your specific country before configuring your payment settings — USDT on Tron is a safe starting point for most African and South Asian markets. Create your NOWPayments account and add wallet addresses for your primary coins. Set up a P2P exchange account — Binance P2P is available in most restricted markets and supports local currency pairs. Deploy your chosen stack: Stack 01 via the Sovereign Blueprint or Stack 02 via the Edge Commerce Stack deployment. Configure the NOWPayments IPN webhook URL in your account settings pointing to your backend endpoint. Run a complete mainnet test transaction and confirm the pipeline end-to-end before promoting. Complete a test P2P conversion with a small amount so you know the process before your first real sale.
